body:
`insight:india-sme-platform-outcomes-reforms` | confidence: verified | date: 2026-10-14

Scale (SEBI, data to 31 Jul 2026): 1,496 entities listed on SME platforms since inception (2012), 365 migrated to main board, Rs40,222 crore raised, combined market cap ~Rs4.71 lakh crore. Boom: FY24 was the record year with 196 SME IPOs raising >Rs6,000 crore; 159 more raised >Rs5,700 crore by 15 Oct 2024 (SEBI board memo, Dec 2024). Abuse documented by SEBI: IPO and rights proceeds 'diverted ... to related / connected parties or to shell companies controlled by promoters', and 'fraudulent sales and purchases through circular transactions amongst related parties' to create positive sentiment; SEBI issued an investor caution on 28 Aug 2024. Reforms approved Dec 2024 and notified in the ICDR amendment of March 2025: minimum application two lots and above Rs2 lakh (from ~Rs1 lakh); OFS capped at 20% of issue size and each seller can sell at most 20% of holding; operating profit of Rs1 crore in 2 of 3 preceding years (the Oct-2026 paper describes the existing test as EBIT); promoter lock-in for MPC raised to 5 years from 3; monitoring agency mandatory above Rs20 crore (from Rs100 crore); IPO only if issue size >Rs10 crore; 2-year cooling-off after conversion from partnership/LLP or change of control. Oct-2026 consultation paper proposes a Rs3 crore average operating profit test but also lowering the Rs2 lakh minimum application and aligning allocation with main board (RII category). Outcomes: tracker data show 58% of 2024 SME IPOs below issue (median -20%) (single-source). Actionable: treat SME listings as presumptively promoter-exit or manipulation vehicles unless cash-flow, auditor and related-party checks pass.

Sources:
- https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/meetingfiles/jan-2025/1735725342588_1.pdf
- https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/oct-2026/1791972839578.pdf
- https://bcajonline.org/journal/redefining-ipo-frameworks-a-detailed-exploration-of-sebis-march-2025-icdr-amendment/
- https://marketping.in/ipo/performance

data.section: 1. S2 checklist, bank form (filled before L1; every rule dated)

title: UTKARSHBNK_live › 1. S2 checklist, bank form (filled before L1; every rule dated)

body:
`review_queue.md` lists each call that needs a human, with its written rule, the reason, the resolver's proposal, and
evidence links with snippets. The reasons are: assisted doc scan, type d judgment, sources disagree, near the
threshold, the company's own figure governs, and **OVERDUE** (resolve_by has passed with no data).
1. Open the evidence link. Apply the **written rule** (memdb `resolution_rule`) strictly. A proposal is a lead, not an
   outcome: the regex catches the *first* number, and that can be H1, a normalised figure, or the prior quarter. Known
   traps: ICICIGI (H1 vs quarter), MPHASIS (the rule wants the reported DSO, not the "normalised" one), and GE (no number is captured; read the snippet).
2. Append one line to `review_decisions.jsonl` (an outcome of 1 or 0 needs a `source`):
   `{"id": "thesis:paper-call:X:y", "outcome": 1, "value": 24.3, "source": "https://…", "source_date": "2027-02-05", "note": "Q3 press release p2", "decided_by": "user"}`
   Use `"void"` only when the source stopped publishing the metric, or when the rule says "not disclosed = void" (for example ENDURANCE driveshaft). Never void a call because it was a miss.
3. Run `resolve.py` again. The decision becomes a seed, and `apply.sh` writes it to memdb.
4. Claude may draft decisions in a session. The user confirms type d calls and anything within the guard of the threshold (`decided_by` records who decided).

body:
| Episode | Run-up before peak | Peak → low | How long to regain the peak |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2008 | — | −33% (Mar→Oct 2008) | 19 months |
| **2011–2015** | **2.8× in 3 years** (2008→2011) | **−45%** ($1,912 → $1,046) | **~9 years** (Jul-2020) |
| 2020–2022 | — | −23% | ~3.5 years |
| **2023–2026 (now)** | **2.9× in 26 months** | **−36% so far** | ? |
| 1980–1982 (widely documented, not in our data) | ~4× in 2 years | ~−65% ($850 → ~$300) | ~28 years nominal |

**The uncomfortable match:** this run-up (2.9× in ~2 years) is almost the same size as 2008–11 (2.8×), which ended in a −45%
fall and a 9-year wait. A Fed that is *hiking* with real yields near 3% is closer to the 1980/2013 setting than to 2008/2020,
when the Fed was cutting.
